name: JWA World Title
epitaph: Keith Wildwing won the title in the fed's own debut PPV, "And Justice For All" (22 August 1999) — a twenty-man battle royal feeding into a ladder match, its own closing pinfall lost to the surviving transcript, but confirmed by "Blind Justice"'s own opening recap package, which shows Wildwing "his body tired and worn" holding the belt. That same recap frames Jon Clark as having then taken the title from Wildwing off-page — a reign this ledger does not structure, since no document dates or stages it directly. At "Blind Justice" itself, Bryan Mercy outlasted Clark in a Triple Threat Ladder Match to become champion, and successfully defended the belt against War at "Dark Justice" (14 November 1999) — the held record's last-attested title change. Two reigns anchor the ledger here: the founding and the last-attested.

name: JWA World Television Title
epitaph: Already a defended title when the held record opens: Oasis is billed defending it against Gangrene at "And Justice For All" (22 August 1999), a match the served part does not itself capture. Jose Gonzalez is billed at "Dark Justice" as "a former two-time JWA TV champion," meaning the belt changed hands at least twice more off-page between the two held shows. By "Dark Justice" (14 November 1999, the held record's last-attested show), Chad Hazzard holds the title and defends it successfully against Gonzalez, with the M.o.A. beating him down after the bell.

name: JWA Trans-Atlantic Title
epitaph: Crowned at the fed's own debut PPV, "And Justice For All" (22 August 1999) — Biff Wellington's own opening line promises "the World, the Trans-Atlantic, and the Hardcore Titles will all find homes tonight" — but the title match itself falls in one of the five unserved parts of that broadcast, so its first champion is not attested by any held document. By "Dark Justice" (14 November 1999, the held record's last-attested show), Matt Attict holds the title and defends it successfully against Preacher, with M.o.A. interference and a run-in from the masked "Mysterio."

name: JWA Hardcore Title
epitaph: Crowned at the fed's own debut PPV, "And Justice For All" (22 August 1999) per Biff Wellington's own opening line, and billed for that night between Faith and Mass Carnage ("the Angel") — Leon Wallace is billed to present the belt to its winner. No document in the held record stages or resolves the match; no reign survives to structure.
